checks.method: Compared v1 design delta against the selected v0 Territory C. Only the circular/track geometry language was replaced; bold asymmetry, palette, copy, left-product/right-copy structure and information rhythm were retained.

Mapped the v0 Territory C product center to a normalized anchor and reused it in the v1 hero. Locked anchor = (0.3203125, 0.5846938776); on the 1440 × 1800 hero this equals (461.25, 1052.44897968) px.

SHA-256 of input and v1 exact product copy both equal 241716aa68e28a113150907d6a0c9b024f2febb7a948b3d01c55959fc032c9f0. Visual inspection confirmed the terracotta color, cylinder, floating lid, black seam and front button remain recognizable and unchanged.

Removed the prior near-complete ring, zigzag waveform and track combination. v1 uses unequal, non-concentric, open cubic-Bezier ribbons plus irregular polygonal clay particles; no copied circle grid or reference-specific geometry is drawn.
Confirmed all four approved phrases appear in the render source and no duration, absolute-silence claim, reference brand name or reference headline appears in the final visual source.
Confirmed one 1440 × 1800 hero, two 1440 × 1200 selling-point modules and one 1440 × 4224 stacked composite.

Inspected the hero and both modules individually at original resolution and inspected the stacked page. Headings and approved copy are legible; geometry does not cover the product or primary text; module boundaries and color continuity are clear; the low-contrast footer copy in module 01 was corrected before final verification.
Compiled the Python render source in memory without syntax errors and executed it successfully to regenerate every v1 PNG.
Computed SHA-256 for every file in outputs/v0 before and after v1 work; the manifests matched exactly.
Parsed outputs/project-state.json successfully as JSON after updating current version, decisions, locks, preserved items, changed items and artifact paths.
